rationale: Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial, observational Parkinson's cohort, or PD animal model has evaluated ground dill seed (Anethum graveolens fruit) on rest tremor severity. Consistent with Round 3 findings across 25 dill-seed symptoms (where only dysmenorrhea pain and labor anxiety showed non-PD clinical signals), existing human dill-seed RCTs address metabolic lipids/glucose (Mousavi 2022) or visceral pain (Heidarifar 2014) without motor, gait, speech, handwriting, or swallowing measures. An older rodent locomotion note (Racz-Kotilla 1996) and a bundled black-sticky-rice plus unspecified-part dill extract stroke trial (Kongbunkiat 2024) neither isolate ground dill seed nor measure Parkinson's rest tremor severity.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial or observational cohort has evaluated dried dill weed (Anethum graveolens leaf) on attention impairment in Parkinson's disease or general populations. A mouse scopolamine-amnesia study (Mesripour 2016, PMID:27168754) used unspecified-part dill essence/aqueous extract in non-PD rodents measuring passive avoidance/object recognition rather than human attention impairment, and a bundled Thai minor-stroke trial (Kongbunkiat 2024) combined black sticky rice with unspecified-part dill extract without isolating dill leaf.

Maybe True (50.005): One double-blind, placebo-controlled human RCT of botanically verified Anethum graveolens LEAF powder (Haidari et al. 2020, PMID:32503652, PMC7275438; n=42 adults with type 2 diabetes randomized to 3 g/day dried dill leaf capsules vs starch placebo for 8 weeks) reported a marked drop in permanent colonic motility disorder symptoms from 11/21 (52.4%) to 1/21 (4.8%) in the dill-leaf arm (within-group chi-square P=0.010), while permanent symptoms remained unchanged at 10/21 (47.6%) to 10/21 (47.6%) in placebo (P=0.317; endpoint Fisher exact P=0.0036). Mechanistically, aerial-part dill extract protected colonic mucosal integrity and microbiota in DSS-colitis mice (Qiao 2025, PMID:39667686), whereas an antidiarrheal rat study (Brinsi 2024, PMID:39115258) tested dill fruit/seed rather than dill weed leaf. Adversarial PubMed screening found no conflicting dill-leaf constipation trial. Confidence remains minimal_signal because Haidari 2020 pooled constipation under 'colonic motility disorders', reported within-group table p-values, enrolled T2D rather than PD patients, and used dried leaf powder rather than fresh dill weed.

Large double-blind soy trials in non-PD adults consistently report null executive and attention outcomes—including the 2.5-year Class I WISH trial (Henderson 2012 PMC3369523, n=313: null on global cognition and executive/attention factors) and a 6-month Alzheimer's RCT (Gleason 2015 PMC4657545, n=65: null)—while a 16-week whole roasted soy-nut crossover (Kleinloog 2021 PMC8634607, n=23) improved regional CBF and psychomotor movement time (-20 ms, p=0.005) with null effects on executive function and memory, and fermented soy powder (West 2025 PMC12472887) was likewise null on executive function and processing speed.

Unknown (Researched): no human trial or observational cohort has evaluated cooked edamame on Parkinson's bradykinesia severity. Unknown (Researched): no controlled trial tests cooked whole edamame for constipation in Parkinson's disease or functional constipation. Maybe True (minimal_signal toward easing): a direct human Parkinson's crossover study (Nagashima 2016, PMID:26810548; n=7 fluctuating PD patients; Adjusted Low RoB in Boelens Keun 2021 PMC8634393) reported an 80% longer acute ON-period (270 vs 150 min, p=0.028) and lower covariate-adjusted 3-OMD (317.0 vs 374.6 ng/mL, p=0.03) when 11 g ground Glycine max soybeans (~4 g protein) were taken with levodopa/carbidopa, with zero opposing soybean clinical trials in live 2020-2026 PubMed searches. Strictly capped at minimal_signal (50.005) and tempered by important dose and matrix caveats: unadjusted levodopa AUC was null, the 3-hour ON window does not equal 24-hour daily off time, a full culinary cup of cooked shelled edamame (~18.5 g protein) supplies >4x the protein tested in Nagashima 2016 (creating theoretical LNAA competition if co-ingested with levodopa per Barichella 2006, despite lower legume LNAA digestibility in Kashyap 2024), and a 2025 Parkinson's UK edamame user reported no noticeable dopaminergic lift.

Minimal directional signal that large or fresh cooked fava bean meals can acutely precipitate anxiety during hyperdopaminergic/dyskinetic reactions in medicated PD patients, supporting the 'worsens' hypothesis as Maybe True. Two independent clinical case reports document acute anxiety alongside generalized dyskinesias and autonomic symptoms (sweating/tachycardia) in PD patients on stable regimens: Lambea-Gil 2021 (PMID:34979720; positive 2-day rechallenge ~90 min after fresh sauteed broad beans) and Ramirez-Moreno 2013/2015 (PMID:24332774; ~2 h after 300-400 g raw/stewed broad beans, with BP 90/55 mm Hg). No clinical study has tested ordinary cooked fava beans on validated PD anxiety scales or shown anxiety reduction. Kept at minimal_signal (50.005) because anxiety occurred secondarily during acute excess-levodopa dyskinetic episodes without a standardized anxiety instrument or plasma L-DOPA assay. Safety caveats: unpredictable L-DOPA content (mature boiled seeds ~0.10-0.76 mg/g dw vs fresh pods ~28.65 mg/g dw; wet heat degrades L-DOPA), peak-dose dyskinesia when added to prescription levodopa, withdrawal NMLS on abrupt cessation (Ladha 2005), non-selective MAOI interaction risk, and acute hemolytic favism in G6PD deficiency.

Minimal directional signal that fenugreek seed extracts may modestly ease anxiety in non-PD adults, supporting the 'reduces' hypothesis as Maybe True. In Hausenblas et al. 2020 (PMID:32441668; NCT03528538), a 60-day double-blind placebo-controlled RCT in 57 healthy young men (mean age 26.1 y) found standardized fenugreek seed extract (400 or 500 mg/d) significantly improved anxiety levels, Aging Male Symptoms, grip strength, and HRQoL vs placebo (p<0.05) with no adverse events, corroborated preclinically by Kalshetti 2015 (PMC4745208; 4-hydroxyisoleucine from fenugreek seeds reduced anxiety-like behavior in stressed OBX rats). Multi-ingredient trials showing anxiety benefits (Kashinath 2026 Fenavari + shatavari; Pandaran Sudheeran 2016 CurQfen + curcumin) are bundled and excluded from attribution, while Steels 2011 (PMID:21312304, Testofen + minerals) found no change in general mood. Major gaps (non-PD healthy young male sample, standardized extract rather than culinary ground seed, small n=19/arm, exact anxiety scores omitted from abstract) keep this strictly at minimal_signal (50.005). Safety caveats: generally well tolerated in trials (Amiri Ardekani 2026 PMC12858439), with mild GI discomfort most common plus hypoglycemia risk (especially with antidiabetics), legume/peanut cross-reactive allergy, maple-syrup odor, and potential CYP3A4/warfarin herb-drug interactions.

Strictly limited to minimal_signal (50.005) due to major gaps: IBHB is a proprietary standardized seed extract rather than culinary toasted fenugreek seed (exposure_fit=remote), Nathan 2014 did not separately publish isolated bradykinesia item scores (outcome_fit=partial), exact between-group p-values/ITT counts are absent from the public abstract, co-authors are industry-affiliated (Indus Biotech), and no independent replication has been published in >12 years. Four independent non-PD human clinical trials of ground/milled flaxseed consistently demonstrate easing—opposing the frozen worsening claim—of constipation severity: Soltanian & Janghorbani (2018 n=53 / 2019 n=77, single IRCT family) showed 20 g/d flaxseed cookies beat placebo and psyllium on Rome III constipation (p=0.002) and stool consistency (p<0.001); Sun 2020 (n=90 Rome IV FC RCT) showed 50 g/d flaxseed flour beat lactulose on Wexner score (14->6.5 vs 15->9, p<0.001), bowel frequency (2->7/wk), and PAC-QOL (-1.34 vs -0.66); Ma 2022 (n=60 elderly FC) and Cunnane 1995 (n=10 crossover, +30% BM/wk) corroborate laxation. Tempering/adversarial evidence includes Amjadi Suraki 2024 (n=70 ICU RCT: 18 g/d flaxseed powder matched magnesium hydroxide on stool consistency/frequency but had slower first-defecation onset 35.2 vs 24.8 h, p=0.023), Lim 2021 (n=33 lung chemoradiation: 40 g/d poorly tolerated without strict hydration), and mixed Parkinson's UK forum accounts (positive dechallenge/rechallenge with golden linseed alongside refractory PD constipation despite flaxseed). Capped at minimal_signal (50.005, Maybe False) per rubric v1 because no controlled clinical trial in diagnosed Parkinson's disease exists; adequate hydration and spacing from oral levodopa are essential.

While patients with Parkinson's neurogenic orthostatic hypotension should monitor standing blood pressure when adding antihypertensive doses of milled flaxseed, seated BP reduction in hypertensives does not establish either easing or worsening of PD orthostatic lightheadedness (Unknown).

Compromised/inconsistent Khalajinia 2024 is explicitly excluded (reliability_fit=unusable). Because rheumatoid, migraine, and mastalgia pain differ mechanistically from Parkinson's musculoskeletal, neuropathic, and dystonic pain and no PD pain RCT exists, confidence is capped strictly at minimal_signal (50.005, Maybe True).

No completed Parkinson's disease trial has reported attention outcomes for ground ginger (recruiting PD trials NCT07882108 and IRCT20251028067794N1 have no posted results). However, independent non-PD human double-blind RCTs of single-agent Zingiber officinale consistently point toward improved attention/concentration: (1) Ashraf et al. 2022 (PMC8794674, DB-RCT n=53 adults with controlled primary hypothyroidism) directly tested pulverized ground ginger rhizome powder capsules (1,000 mg/day for 30 days) and reported significant reduction in ThySRQ concentration disturbance (1.29+/-0.91 to 0.58+/-0.72 vs placebo 1.07+/-0.81 to 1.05+/-0.85, p=0.002), though concurrent TSH lowering could confound symptom change; (2) Saenghong et al. 2012 (PMC3253463, DB-RCT n=60 healthy middle-aged women) showed 800 mg/day standardized ethanolic ginger extract for 2 months significantly improved auditory oddball N100 amplitude (p=0.0014), P300 latency (p=0.0004), P300 amplitude (p=0.0020), digit vigilance accuracy (p=0.0217) and false alarms (p<0.01), and choice reaction time accuracy (p<0.0001) and speed (p=0.0178); and (3) Victoria-Montesinos et al. 2026 (PMC13198985, 18-RCT Zingiberaceae MA) additionally documented Nakamura et al. 2025 (DB-RCT n=88, 6-shogaol ginger extract improving Cognitrax Complex Attention). Crucial adversarial caveat: Victoria-Montesinos 2026 found NO significant pooled effect on attention/inhibitory control across 3 pooled Zingiberaceae trials dominated by curcumin (SMD -0.07, 95% CI -0.33 to 0.18, p=0.58) and graded cognitive certainty very low. Because all ginger-specific attention RCTs lean eases—including a ground-ginger powder DB-RCT—this earns minimal_signal (Maybe True).

No completed human clinical trial, observational cohort, or controlled PD study has evaluated whether ground ginger worsens bradykinesia severity. Comprehensive review of 109 human ginger RCTs (Anh et al. 2020, PMC7019938) confirms no completed Parkinson's disease symptom trials, and both active PD ginger registrations (NCT07882108 n=72 two-dose extract capsules; IRCT20251028067794N1 n=48 1,000 mg/d powder tablets) list composite MDS-UPDRS without posted results or standalone bradykinesia severity estimates. Preclinical rodent toxin models of isolated ginger phenolics (6-shogaol, 6-gingerol, zingerone) are also mixed by timing—Kabuto 2011 (PMID:21769642) found post-treatment zingerone worsened striatal dopamine loss in 6-OHDA mice. Evidence for ground ginger on bradykinesia severity in PD therefore remains Unknown (Researched).

No clinical study has measured levodopa pharmacokinetics or Parkinson's daily OFF time with grated ginger. Mechanistically, gastric emptying affects levodopa absorption, and small capsule trials in non-PD adults showed mixed gastric emptying results: Wu et al. 2008 (n=24 healthy) and Hu et al. 2011 (n=11 functional dyspepsia) found 1.2 g ginger capsules accelerated soup gastric half-emptying (13.1 vs 26.7 min; 12.3 vs 16.1 min), whereas Stewart et al. 1991 (n=28) found no gastric emptying change at 500 mg—and none measured levodopa blood levels or PD motor fluctuations. Recruiting PD trials NCT07882108 (ghrelin/gut function/MDS-UPDRS I-IV) and IRCT20251028067794N1 have no posted results. Verdict remains Unknown (Researched).

No placebo-controlled trial has tested pickled ginger for daytime sleepiness in Parkinson's disease or other populations. Yamprasert et al. 2020 (PMID:32312261, PMC7171779, DB-RCT n=80 allergic rhinitis) found 500 mg ginger extract caused less drowsiness than the antihistamine loratadine, but had no placebo arm so lower sedation reflects avoiding loratadine rather than wake promotion. Verdict remains Unknown (Researched).

All three single-agent oral Zingiber officinale double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs measuring depressive symptoms were strictly NULL: Crichton et al. 2024 (PMID:37699474, n=103 chemotherapy) found no effect on HADS depression; Ashraf et al. 2022 (PMC8794674, n=53 hypothyroidism) found no significant improvement in depressed/low mood (1.54+/-1.06 vs 1.82+/-1.12, p=0.188); and Crichton et al. 2023 (PMID:37690779, n=51 healthy adults) found no DASS-21 depression difference. Positive mood trials involved different botanical species (de Queiroz 2024 Zingiber zerumbet) or multi-herb combinations, and no trial tested pickled ginger or PD depression. Verdict remains Unknown (Researched).

No clinical study has tested oral grated ginger for Parkinson's sialorrhea/drooling. While sialagogue mouthwashes in xerostomia suggest oral ginger pungency may stimulate salivation (opposite to reducing drooling), topical rinses in dry-mouth patients do not transfer to oral grated ginger in PD sialorrhea (which primarily reflects impaired swallowing clearance). No clinical trial has tested pickled ginger or evaluated fatigue in people with Parkinson's disease. However, three independent placebo-controlled human DB-RCTs of oral Zingiber officinale root powder capsules demonstrate statistically significant reductions in fatigue or perceived exertion in fatigued/exerted cohorts: (1) Crichton et al. 2024 (PMID:37699474, multicenter DB-RCT n=103 chemotherapy-naive adults) showed 1.2 g/day standardized ginger root powder (84 mg/day gingerols/shogaols) across 3 chemotherapy cycles significantly improved fatigue vs placebo (F(1,101)=10.11, p=0.002, partial eta2=0.09, surviving Bonferroni correction; consistent with Crichton 2019 MA OR 0.20, p=0.03); (2) Ashraf et al. 2022 (PMC8794674, DB-RCT n=53 primary hypothyroidism) showed 1,000 mg/day ginger powder for 30 days reduced ThySRQ tiredness (2.19->0.73 vs placebo 2.31->2.36, p<0.001); and (3) Lage et al. 2026 (PMC13510715, DB-RCT n=32 CrossFit athletes) showed 2 g/day ginger for 9 days lowered Borg RPE (5.2 vs 6.8, p<0.001) and preserved peak-force neuromuscular fatigue index (p=0.015). Conflicting/null evidence: Crichton et al. 2023 (PMID:37690779, DB-RCT n=51 healthy young adults aged 18-30 y) found NO fatigue difference over 14 days in a low-fatigue healthy cohort; in athletic endurance, Kurtz et al. 2026 (PMID:42043058, DB-crossover n=30 trained cyclists, 4 wk) found NO difference in 75-km cycling time, RPE, or muscle soreness, and Demirli et al. 2025 (PMID:41010475, DB-crossover n=16 active men, 1,000 mg acute) found ginger alone did NOT improve time-to-exhaustion or RPE; and Higashikawa 2024 (PMC11357383, n=100) assessed localized eye fatigue only. Kept at minimal_signal because both clinical-disease fatigue DB-RCTs (chemotherapy n=103, hypothyroidism n=53) and Lage 2026 consistently favored fatigue reduction (outweighing null healthy/athletic endurance trials), while pickled ginger (acetic acid/sugar brine matrix) differs substantially from dried standardized root powder capsules and no PD fatigue trial exists.

No clinical study has tested grated ginger for Parkinson's dysarthria or speech intelligibility. In Ashraf et al. 2022 (PMC8794674, DB-RCT n=53 hypothyroidism, 1,000 mg/day ginger powder for 30 days), self-reported speech change was strictly NULL versus placebo (p=0.421). Recruiting PD trials NCT07882108 and IRCT20251028067794N1 have no posted speech results. Verdict remains Unknown (Researched).

Controlled human evidence on ginger and swallowing is small, heterogeneous, and conflicting, with zero single-agent Parkinson's disease dysphagia trials. Two tiny acute healthy-volunteer studies suggested acute oropharyngeal stimulation: Hirata et al. 2016 (PMID:27374286, n=18 healthy older adults 63-90 y) reported increased salivary substance P and endoscopic swallowing scores 15 minutes after 1% ginger orally disintegrating tablets vs placebo (p<0.05), and Krival & Bates 2012 (PMID:21811834, n=20 healthy young women) observed higher linguapalatal pressure with carbonated ginger brew vs club soda/water (p<0.001). Conversely, the ONLY multi-week neurological DB-RCT measuring clinical dysphagia severity (Foshati et al. 2023, PMC10605938, n=52 RRMS, 1,500 mg/day ginger tablets x 12 weeks) was strictly NULL for both dysphagia frequency (p=0.44) and severity (p=0.44, low baseline scores), and the study closest to culinary ground ginger (Lohsiriwat et al. 2010, PMID:20420113, n=14 healthy men, 1 g dried ground ginger in water, fixed-order) reported increased LES relaxation (p=0.003) alongside DECREASED esophageal peristaltic propagation velocity (3.47 to 2.85 cm/s, p=0.018). In PD itself, Iwasaki 2000 (PMID:10969718) shortened swallowing reflex latency with the 5-herb Kampo formula Banxia Houpo Tang (cannot isolate ginger). Because acute non-dysphagic ODT/beverage physiology is balanced by a null 12-week neurological dysphagia DB-RCT and slowed esophageal peristalsis with ground ginger, this claim stays Unknown (Researched).

No clinical study has measured walking speed or gait slowness with grated ginger in Parkinson's disease. Foshati et al. 2023 (PMID:36974730, DB-RCT n=52 RRMS) reported improved composite MS disability scores (EDSS -0.54 vs +0.08, p<0.001; MSIS-29 physical p=0.001) with 1,500 mg/day ginger tablets, but did not report timed walking speed—and Broeckel et al. 2025 (PMID:40732990, DB-RCT n=30 joint pain, supercritical CO2/fermented ginger extract) found an inconclusive multivariate WOMAC pain/stiffness/function test (p=0.690). Recruiting PD trials NCT07882108 and IRCT20251028067794N1 have no posted results. Because composite MS EDSS is not a PD gait-speed outcome and extract/tablet trials conflict with null WOMAC function, this claim remains Unknown (Researched).

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial tests frozen grapes, grape juice, or grape extracts on clinical apathy (e.g., Starkstein Apathy Scale, AES) in Parkinson disease or other cohorts. Calapai 2017 (PMID:29163162, n=111) measured depression/anxiety rather than apathy, and Haskell-Ramsay 2017 (PMID:28429081) found null Bond-Lader alertness/contentment.

Maybe False (minimal_signal toward easing): three independent human double-blind placebo-controlled trials of purple grape juice or standardized Vitis vinifera red grape juice extract report statistically significant improvements on objective attention tasks outside Parkinson disease, with zero trials showing worsening—Haskell-Ramsay 2017 (PMID:28429081, n=16 analyzed crossover, 230 mL purple grape juice: faster composite attention RT F=4.79, p=0.047, accuracy null p=0.472), Calapai 2017 (PMID:29163162, n=111 older adults 56-75 y, 12 wk 250 mg/d Cognigrape: RBANS attention p<0.001 vs placebo), and Amone 2024 (PMID:39335927, n=96 completers, 84 d 250 mg/d Cognigrape: Modified Bells selective attention +8.8% vs +4.9% at 90 min p=0.001; RBANS attention p<0.05 at D28 and vs placebo at D84, one-tailed tests), supported by Bird 2022 systematic review (PMID:34041549). Tempered by competing null attention outcomes in Lamport 2016 (n=25 Concord juice RVIP null), Helmer 2020 (n=31 Gulf War Illness CPT-3 detectability p=0.10 null), Lee 2017 (n=10 whole grape powder 6 mo: null between-group neuropsych battery despite FDG-PET preservation), Bell 2022 (n=60 GSPE seed extract null), Wang 2023 pooled fruit meta-analysis, juice/extract vs whole frozen-grape gap, and absence of any Parkinson attention RCT.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial tests frozen grapes or grape juice on Parkinson bradykinesia (UPDRS motor bradykinesia subscores). Oliveira 2020 (PMID:32798568, n=19 PD patients) recorded UPDRS motor scores only at baseline and found null incremental TUG/6MWT changes (p=0.11-0.28). Preclinical studies test isolated compounds (rhapontigenin in MPTP mice, PMID:40913726) or grape seed extract (Sarkaki 2012, PMC4075680), which are remote from frozen table grapes.

Unknown (Researched): no human clinical trial has tested frozen or fresh whole grapes on chronic constipation or Parkinson bowel motility (dried raisins are a distinct high-fiber matrix and excluded). Eftekhar et al. 2026 (PMID:42356234, n=21 uncontrolled Crohn disease pilot, 45 g/d freeze-dried grape powder 21 d) showed good tolerability and modest microbiome shifts without constipation outcomes, and Erickson et al. 2017 (PMID:28342683, n=40 crossover) showed low breath hydrogen with white grape juice vs apple juice without bowel-frequency endpoints. Public Parkinson UK forum reports are mixed (one peer recommended grapes with fluids, while a 2023 caregiver noted 3-day PD constipation persisting despite daily grapes, other fruit, flaxseed, and prescription laxatives).

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial or pharmacokinetic study evaluates frozen grapes or grape juice on levodopa absorption, motor fluctuations, or daily OFF time in Parkinson disease. Unlike protein-rich dairy or CYP3A4-inhibiting grapefruit, culinary grapes have minimal protein (~0.7 g/100 g) and lack established clinical levodopa interactions; Oliveira 2020 (PMID:32798568) did not measure OFF time.

Maybe True (minimal_signal toward easing, strictly aligned with Round 1 grape anxiety precedent 0860): one double-blind placebo-controlled 12-week trial in 111 healthy older adults aged 56-75 y (Calapai 2017, PMID:29163162, PMC5671585) reported a statistically significant -15.8% reduction in Beck Depression Inventory (BDI-13) scores with 250 mg/day standardized Vitis vinifera red grape juice extract (Cognigrape) vs placebo (p<0.0001), alongside acute calm gains from purple grape juice (Haskell-Ramsay 2017, p=0.046) and zero trials showing depressive worsening. Strongly tempered by subclinical baseline BDI (mean 4.52 +/- 0.97, non-depressed healthy older adults), standardized extract rather than frozen whole grapes, competing null depression/mood outcomes in Krikorian 2010 (PMID:20028599, n=12 MCI Concord grape juice: null GDS depressive symptoms), Hendrickson 2008 (PMID:19158941, n=35 acute grape juice mood null), Helmer 2020 (PMID:32438639, n=31 Gulf War Illness: baseline PHQ-8 recorded without mood efficacy gain), Colombage 2026 flavonoid mood SR finding no chronic whole-grape mood RCT benefits, pending whole-grape-powder HAM-D trial NCT07214428 (n=50), and zero Parkinson depression trials.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial, observational cohort, or animal study has evaluated frozen grapes or grape polyphenols on REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) or dream enactment frequency. Trzepizur 2018 (PMID:29659956, n=40 OSA) found unchanged polysomnographic sleep-stage distribution with grape-juice polyphenol capsules without measuring REM atonia or dream enactment.

Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial has evaluated raw grapes or grape juice for sialorrhea/drooling in Parkinson disease or any other clinical population. Public Parkinson UK forum threads (2011, 2012, 2023) document an informal nursing/peer practical tip recommending diluted dark/black grape juice (alongside pineapple juice) for nighttime drooling and morning throat clearing, with one patient reporting subjective benefit, but anecdotal liquid-juice tips cannot establish clinical efficacy for raw grapes.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial or preclinical levodopa-induced dyskinesia (LID) study evaluates frozen grapes on Parkinson dyskinesia severity. Oliveira 2020 (PMID:32798568) did not report dyskinesia outcomes, and rodent 6-OHDA/MPTP grape seed extract or isolated stilbenoid studies did not model levodopa-induced dyskinesia.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial, observational study, or experimental model evaluates raw grapes on Parkinson dystonia severity (OFF-period foot dystonia or peak-dose dystonia). Both the PD grape-juice exercise trial (Oliveira 2020) and preclinical grape-seed/stilbenoid models omit dystonia outcomes.

Maybe True (minimal_signal toward easing): multiple independent human double-blind placebo-controlled trials of Concord grape juice or standardized Vitis vinifera grape juice extract report statistically significant improvements on executive or frontostriatal interference-control subtasks outside Parkinson disease, with zero trials showing worsening—Helmer 2020 (PMID:32438639, n=31/36 Gulf War Illness 24 wk 16 oz/d Concord grape juice: baseline-adjusted Halstead Category Test RCAT improved +8.4 T-score points vs placebo p=0.04, correlating with serum epicatechin-sulfate r=0.48 p=0.01 and petunidin-glucuronide r=0.53 p<0.01 in PMID:34237311, though unadjusted RCAT p=0.10 and Stroop p=0.21 were null), Krikorian 2012 (PMID:22468945, n=21 MCI 16 wk Concord juice: reduced semantic interference with increased right prefrontal/posterior fMRI activation), Lamport 2016 (PMID:26864371, n=25 crossover 12 wk 355 mL/d Concord juice: improved complex 25-min driving simulator performance and immediate spatial memory), and Amone 2024 (PMID:39335927, n=96 completers 84 d 250 mg/d Cognigrape: improved executive-inclusive ENB-2 total scores vs placebo p<0.001, one-tailed tests), corroborated by Bird 2022 systematic review (PMID:34041549). Constrained strictly to minimal_signal (50.005) by unadjusted/Stroop nulls in Helmer 2020, null between-group neuropsych battery in Lee 2017 (n=10 whole grape powder 6 mo despite preserved prefrontal FDG-PET p<0.01), null GSPE trial (Bell 2022 n=60), Wang 2023 pooled fruit meta-analysis, juice/extract vs whole frozen-grape gap, and zero Parkinson executive trials.

Unknown (Researched): in the only direct human Parkinson disease grape trial, Oliveira et al. 2020 (PMID:32798568, n=24 randomized / 19 analyzed, 4 wk aquatic exercise +/- 400 mL/d Vitis labrusca grape juice), Berg Balance Scale group-by-time comparison was completely null (p=0.70), and no trial has tested whole frozen grapes on Parkinson fall frequency. Berg Balance Scale is a balance performance proxy separate from prospective counted falls, and showed no incremental grape-juice benefit (p=0.70).

Unknown (Researched): human clinical trials of grape juice on pathological or perceived fatigue are null, outweighing acute athletic endurance outcomes. Helmer et al. 2020 (PMID:32438639, n=31 completers, 24 wk 16 oz/d Concord grape juice DB-RCT in Gulf War Illness—a chronic fatigue disorder) found NO effect on PHQ-15 fatigue (p=0.67), and Niknam et al. 2025 (PMID:40584107, n=22 soccer crossover DB-RCT) likewise found NO effect on perceived fatigue (p>0.05) despite longer exercise time-to-exhaustion (p<0.001). Acute runner time-to-exhaustion (Toscano 2020 n=14, p=0.008; de Sousa 2022 n=47) and judo strength (Goulart 2020 n=20) reflect carbohydrate/polyphenol athletic ergogenics rather than persistent Parkinson fatigue, and isolated resveratrol was null on multiple sclerosis fatigue (Keramatzadeh 2025, n=55).

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial tests frozen grapes or grape juice on freezing of gait (FOG) in Parkinson disease. Oliveira 2020 (PMID:32798568, n=19 PD patients) measured Timed Up and Go (p=0.28 null) and 6-minute walk (p=0.11 null) without reporting freezing-of-gait episodes or NFOG-Q scores.

Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial tests whole raw grapes or grape juice on insomnia or Parkinson sleep initiation/maintenance. Two isolated-extract studies point in opposite directions across non-transferable populations and matrices: Trzepizur et al. 2018 (PMID:29659956, n=40 severe obstructive sleep apnea DB-RCT, 300 mg/d grape juice polyphenol capsules 1 mo) reported a secondary -10 min decrease in polysomnographic total sleep time vs +15 min placebo (p=0.02, sleep stages unchanged), whereas Terauchi et al. 2014 (PMID:24518152, n=91 menopausal women DB-RCT, 200 mg/d isolated grape seed proanthocyanidin extract GSPE 8 wk) reduced Athens Insomnia Scale scores. Neither tests whole raw grapes or PD insomnia.

Unknown (Researched): No clinical trial, observational cohort, or cultural record evaluates frozen grapes on Parkinson hypophonia or vocal intensity (dB SPL). Across Oracle catalog rev 283 and live PubMed/ClinicalTrials.gov sweeps, zero trials link table grapes or grape products to voice loudness.

Unknown (Researched): No clinical trial tests dietary frozen grapes on hyposmia or olfactory identification in Parkinson disease (note PMID:34667313 used grape scent strictly as a diagnostic scratch-and-sniff stimulus in COVID-19 rather than a dietary intervention). Neither clinical grape trials nor PD cohorts report olfactory recovery.

Unknown (Researched): although meta-analysis of 30 RCTs (Ashoori et al. 2023, PMID:37482483) found a small resting systolic BP reduction with whole grape products (WMD -2.69 mmHg, p=0.01, low certainty; grape juice subgroup and DBP/HR null), a rigorous 24-hour ambulatory BP crossover trial of Concord grape juice in 64 prehypertensive/stage-1 hypertensive adults was completely null on primary 24-h SBP and DBP (Dohadwala et al. 2010, PMID:20844075), and Neto et al. 2017 (PMID:28853994, n=26) found no overall resting BP or post-exercise hypotension change (only a post-hoc controlled-BP subgroup dipped). Zero clinical trials or case reports link raw grape intake to orthostatic blood pressure drops, dizziness, or lightheadedness in Parkinson disease or older adults.

Unknown (Researched): no peer-reviewed human randomized clinical trial demonstrates that eating raw grapes eases or worsens clinical pain or Parkinson pain. In Helmer et al. 2020 (PMID:32438639, n=31/36 Gulf War Illness 24 wk Concord grape juice DB-RCT), baseline McGill Pain Questionnaire scores were collected without any statistically significant pain improvement over placebo. An often-cited 16-week freeze-dried grape powder knee osteoarthritis trial (Juma et al., n=72) appears only as an unverified conference abstract (FASEB J 2014) without a full peer-reviewed PubMed-indexed report, and preclinical osteoarthritis models used isolated grape-seed proanthocyanidins or skin extracellular vesicles rather than whole raw grapes.

Unknown (Researched): in the only direct human Parkinson disease grape trial, Oliveira et al. 2020 (PMID:32798568, n=24 randomized / 19 analyzed, 4 wk aquatic exercise +/- 400 mL/d Vitis labrusca grape juice), Berg Balance Scale group-by-time comparison was completely null (p=0.70), and no trial has tested whole raw grapes on Parkinson postural instability severity. Berg Balance Scale directly assesses functional balance/postural stability in PD and showed no incremental benefit from 400 mL/d V. labrusca purple grape juice over aquatic exercise alone (group x time p=0.70).

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial, case series, or preclinical study evaluates frozen grapes on Parkinson hypomimia (reduced facial expressiveness). Oliveira 2020 (PMID:32798568) collected UPDRS motor scores only at baseline without facial-expression subscore follow-up.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial evaluates raw grapes on Parkinson rest tremor severity. Oliveira 2020 (PMID:32798568, n=19 PD patients) recorded UPDRS motor scores at baseline only without tremor follow-up, and rodent 6-OHDA grape seed extract (Sarkaki 2012, PMC4075680) and red-grape-juice rotation (PMC4075659) studies measured rigidity or apomorphine turning rather than resting tremor.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial directly measures stride or step length after raw grape consumption in Parkinson disease. Oliveira 2020 (PMID:32798568, n=19 PD patients) reported null incremental 6-minute walk (p=0.11) and TUG (p=0.28) with purple grape juice without spatiotemporal stride-length metrics, and Mendez 2025 (PMID:40407719, n=15 postmenopausal women) measured overall gait speed rather than Parkinson stride length.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial or experimental study evaluates frozen grapes on Parkinson micrographia (small handwriting). Round 1 hand-function grape trials (Lamport 2016 Concord juice Grooved Pegboard, Bell 2020 GSPE finger tapping) tested non-PD manual speed/dexterity with conflicting/remote results and did not measure handwriting size.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial evaluates frozen grapes on Parkinson dysarthria or speech intelligibility. Cognitive grape-extract trials (Calapai 2017 PMID:29163162, Amone 2024 PMID:39335927) measured RBANS lexical/semantic language subtests in healthy older adults rather than motor speech articulation or intelligibility.

Unknown (Researched): No clinical trial tests frozen grapes on Parkinson dysphagia or swallowing safety. Although Parkinson UK forum users share anecdotal tips for diluted dark grape juice to thin secretions/throat clearing (2011/2012), whole or frozen grapes pose a mechanical texture/choking consideration in dysphagia without any clinical swallowing trial.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial or cohort study evaluates frozen grapes or grape juice on overactive bladder or Parkinson urinary urgency frequency. Urinary grape studies in PubMed solely quantify urinary anthocyanin/polyphenol metabolite excretion rather than lower urinary tract symptoms, and Ha 2025 (PMID:40105788) found no consistent dietary bladder-irritant signal for non-caffeinated fruit.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial, observational cohort, or case series evaluates frozen grapes on visual hallucinations or Parkinson disease psychosis. Preclinical rotenone/currant models (Tsarouchi 2022, PMC9820698) assessed anxiety-like behavior rather than hallucinations, and human cognitive grape trials excluded psychotic disorders.

Unknown (Researched): direct clinical evidence in Parkinson disease is null and balances a small non-PD pilot. Oliveira et al. 2020 (PMID:32798568, n=24 randomized / 19 analyzed PD patients, 4 wk aquatic exercise +/- 400 mL/d Vitis labrusca purple grape juice) found NO incremental benefit of grape juice on 6-Minute Walk Test distance (group x time p=0.11) or Timed Up and Go mobility (p=0.28). Although Mendez et al. 2025 (PMID:40407719, n=15 healthy postmenopausal women, 6 wk freeze-dried whole grape powder DB-RCT) reported faster age-adjusted gait speed and higher grip strength vs control, a tiny non-PD sarcopenia pilot cannot outweigh a null direct Parkinson gait/mobility trial without a dedicated whole-raw-grape PD RCT.

Unknown (Researched): No oral raw grapefruit clinical trial evaluates anxiety severity. Ozer 2025 (PMID:40312670, n=90 PMS) and Czakert 2024 (PMID:38898054, n=486 dental) tested INHALED grapefruit essential oil aromatherapy (exposure_fit=unusable for oral fruit), while Lilja 1998 (PMID:9871430) showed grapefruit raises buspirone AUC 9.2-fold and Yasui 2000 (PMID:10907671) found alprazolam clinical anxiety unaffected.

Unknown (Researched): No clinical trial or observational study evaluates oral raw grapefruit on apathy severity in Parkinson disease or any cohort; clinical grapefruit studies address CYP3A4 pharmacokinetics and cardiometabolic risk factors.

Unknown (Researched): No clinical trial evaluates oral raw grapefruit alone on attention impairment. Psychomotor/DSST declines in Hukkinen 1995, Kupferschmidt 1995, and Lilja 2000 reflect acute sedative drug potentiation (triazolam/midazolam) rather than standalone grapefruit attention effects, while Ede Sarikaya 2026 (PMID:42011111) tested a 5-oil inhaled aromatherapy blend (exposure_fit=unusable).

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial evaluates raw grapefruit on Parkinson bradykinesia. Nagai 2005 cabergoline PK (n=5 PD) reported no motor scores, and rodent neurotoxin studies used isolated compounds (oral limonin in 6-OHDA rats, PMID:37536186; nootkatone in MPTP mice, PMID:38001852; injected naringin, PMID:24797334) that are remote from dietary raw grapefruit.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial tests raw grapefruit on chronic or Parkinson constipation (PMID:41262328 tested a grapefruit-flavored polyethylene glycol laxative rather than grapefruit fruit).

Unknown (Researched): although Nagai et al. 2005 reported ~1.7-fold higher plasma cabergoline concentrations in 5 Parkinson patients taking grapefruit juice without measured motor or OFF-time outcomes (and Aurinsalo 2026, PMID:41390976, showed repeated grapefruit inhibits CYP2B6/2C9/2C19/3A4 in healthy adults), no human trial demonstrates that raw grapefruit reduces or worsens daily OFF time or alters levodopa pharmacokinetics. A February 2026 Parkinson UK forum user reported self-experimenting with grapefruit juice alongside Stalevo (levodopa/carbidopa/entacapone) with minimal perceived benefit not worth continuing while warning of drug-interaction hazards.

Maybe False (minimal_signal toward worsening via CYP3A4 sedative/antipsychotic drug interactions): human randomized crossover trials directly demonstrate that grapefruit CYP3A4 inhibition (bridged to unprocessed raw fruit segments by Bailey 2000, PMID:11103749) significantly enhances drowsiness and sedative psychomotor impairment when co-ingested with CYP3A4-metabolized hypnotics/sedatives—Hukkinen 1995 (PMID:7648762, n=10 crossover: triazolam AUC 1.5x p<0.001, drowsiness significantly enhanced p<0.05), Lilja 2000 (PMID:11009051, n=12 4-phase crossover: repeated grapefruit increased triazolam AUC +143% p<0.001, t1/2 +54%, and worsened subjective drowsiness p<0.05 and DSST p<0.05), Kupferschmidt 1995 (PMID:7628179, n=8 crossover: oral midazolam bioavailability 24%->35% p<0.01, prolonged reaction-time/DSST impairment), and Lilja 1998 (PMID:9871430, n=10: buspirone AUC 9.2x, subjective drug effect p<0.01)—alongside a clinical case report of grapefruit cleanse mimicking overdose of the sedating Parkinson antipsychotic quetiapine (Cinderella 2021, PMID:34608881) and CMAJ pharmacovigilance warnings (Bailey 2013, PMID:23184849). Tempered by substrate- and timing-specific null trials (Yasui 2000, PMID:10907671, n=19: high-bioavailability alprazolam unaffected; Vanakoski 1996, PMID:8858279: single-dose early 30-90 min subjective drowsiness null though DSS impaired p<0.05), zero studies showing standalone raw grapefruit causes or reduces sleepiness without interacting drugs, exclusion of inhaled grapefruit-oil aromatherapy blends (Ede Sarikaya 2026, PMID:42011111, exposure_fit=unusable), and absence of a direct PD daytime-sleepiness trial.

Unknown (Researched): No oral raw grapefruit clinical trial evaluates depression severity. Lee 1999 (PMID:10890261, n=5 depressed adults) showed grapefruit juice raised sertraline trough levels (13.7 to 20.2 ug/L, p=0.047) without reporting depression rating scales, and Ozer 2025 (PMID:40312670) tested inhaled grapefruit essential oil aromatherapy (exposure_fit=unusable).

Unknown (Researched): No clinical trial or case report evaluates oral raw grapefruit on REM sleep behavior disorder or dream enactment frequency in Parkinson disease (even though clonazepam is partly CYP3A4-metabolized, no clinical RBD interaction trial exists).

Unknown (Researched): No clinical trial evaluates raw grapefruit on Parkinson drooling or sialorrhea. O Gallagher et al. 2021 (PMID:32520418, n=11) observed slightly lower saliva volume (-0.34 mL/min) when adding grapefruit juice vs water to nitrate-rich beetroot juice as a secondary biochemical biomarker, not as a clinical drooling test of raw fruit.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial tests raw grapefruit on Parkinson levodopa-induced dyskinesia. Although Nagai 2005 showed ~1.7x plasma cabergoline in 5 PD patients (without adverse events or dyskinesia ratings) and online commentary warns of theoretical erratic medication exposure, no clinical dyskinesia data exist.
Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial, case series, or animal study evaluates raw grapefruit on Parkinson dystonia severity.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial evaluates oral raw grapefruit alone on executive function. Preclinical isolated sinapic acid (scopolamine rats, PMID:36979237) and inhaled 5-oil aromatherapy blends (Ede Sarikaya 2026, PMID:42011111) do not transfer to dietary raw grapefruit.

Unknown (Researched): No clinical trial or cohort study directly measures fall counts or fall incidence after raw grapefruit intake in Parkinson disease. While CYP3A4 hypotensive/sedative drug interactions (Dresser 2000, Hukkinen 1995, Cinderella 2021) plausibly elevate fall risk indirectly when combined with interacting drugs, no clinical study reports fall-frequency outcomes.

Unknown (Researched): No oral raw grapefruit clinical trial evaluates fatigue severity. Ozer 2025 (PMID:40312670) tested inhaled grapefruit essential oil aromatherapy for PMS fatigue (exposure_fit=unusable for oral fruit), and no human fresh-grapefruit trial reports clinical fatigue.
Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial or Parkinson cohort evaluates raw grapefruit on freezing of gait; Nagai 2005 (n=5 PD cabergoline PK) omitted gait/FOG outcomes.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial evaluates oral raw grapefruit on hand dexterity in Parkinson disease; sedative-interaction psychomotor tests (DSST in Lilja 2000) reflect hypnotic potentiation rather than standalone fruit dexterity effects.

Unknown (Researched): No oral raw grapefruit clinical trial evaluates insomnia severity. Both Ozer 2025 (PMID:40312670, PMS sleep changes) and Ede Sarikaya 2026 (PMID:42011111, older-adult 5-oil blend) tested INHALED essential oil aromatherapy (exposure_fit=unusable for oral raw grapefruit).
Unknown (Researched): Zero clinical, observational, or experiential studies evaluate raw grapefruit on Parkinson hypophonia or vocal volume.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial evaluates raw grapefruit on Parkinson muscle rigidity. Nagai 2005 (n=5 PD cabergoline PK) reported no motor rigidity outcomes, a 2026 Reddit comment describing possible stiffness after a grapefruit-flavored sports drink was heavily confounded by strenuous exercise and unknown grapefruit content, and rodent models used isolated parenteral naringin or pure limonin/nootkatone (exposure_fit=remote).

Unknown (Researched): No oral raw grapefruit clinical trial evaluates olfactory impairment or hyposmia in Parkinson disease (registered trial NCT06488807 uses aromatic olfactory enrichment rather than oral fruit).

Maybe False (minimal_signal toward worsening via CYP3A4 hypotensive drug interactions and modest SBP lowering): randomized crossover trials confirm unprocessed raw grapefruit segments (Bailey 2000, PMID:11103749: ~3-fold felodipine AUC) and fresh raw pulp (Ohtani 2002, PMID:12040751, n=8: 1.3-1.5x nifedipine/nisoldipine exposure) irreversibly inhibit intestinal CYP3A4 like grapefruit juice, precipitating excessive blood-pressure reductions, reflex tachycardia, and vasodilatory/hypotensive adverse events across multiple controlled human trials including elderly adults aged 70-83 y (Dresser & Bailey 2000, PMID:10945313, n=12: 2.9x AUC, 4.0x Cmax, lower SBP/DBP and elevated HR; Bailey 1991 Lancet, PMID:1671113, n=6: 284% bioavailability, lower DBP, higher HR, more vasodilatory side effects; Lundahl 1998, PMID:9591935, n=12: additional DBP drop, tachycardia, more vascular adverse events; Takanaga 2000, PMID:10741622, n=8 nisoldipine: lower SBP/DBP), plus clinical case toxicity with the PD antipsychotic quetiapine (Cinderella 2021, PMID:34608881, potent alpha-1 orthostatic agent) and CMAJ clinical pharmacology guidance (Bailey 2013, PMID:23184849). Even without interacting drugs, grapefruit modestly lowers resting SBP in meta-analysis (Onakpoya 2017, PMID:25880021, 3 RCTs n=250: MD -2.43 mmHg, 95% CI -4.77 to -0.09, including Dow 2012 whole fresh grapefruit within-arm -3.21 mmHg p=0.03, between-group null). Constrained to minimal_signal (50.005) because clinically significant hypotensive lightheadedness is conditional on co-ingested CYP3A4-metabolized drugs (amlodipine interaction minimal in Josefsson 1996; Sai 2026 acute crossover differential null) and no trial directly measures standing orthostatic BP in Parkinson disease.

Unknown (Researched): No oral raw grapefruit clinical trial evaluates pain severity. Ozer 2025 (PMID:40312670, n=90 PMS) tested INHALED grapefruit essential oil aromatherapy (exposure_fit=unusable for oral raw fruit), and clinical opioid-interaction trials (Kharasch 2004, PMID:15371986 methadone and PMID:15329598 oral transmucosal fentanyl) found grapefruit juice had NO significant effect on plasma methadone or acute peak fentanyl clinical effects.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial evaluates raw grapefruit on Parkinson postural instability or balance; preclinical isolated-phytochemical rodent studies (nootkatone, limonin, naringin) are remote from oral fruit in PD.
Unknown (Researched): Zero clinical, observational, or experiential studies evaluate raw grapefruit on Parkinson hypomimia (reduced facial expressiveness).
Unknown (Researched): Zero clinical, observational, or preclinical studies evaluate raw grapefruit on Parkinson micrographia (small handwriting).
Unknown (Researched): Zero clinical, observational, or experiential studies evaluate raw grapefruit on Parkinson dysarthria or speech intelligibility.

Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial evaluates raw grapefruit on Parkinson swallowing physiology or dysphagia severity. A firsthand June 2016 Parkinson UK forum post documents an acute breakfast choking and syncope episode when a large piece of raw grapefruit lodged in a PD patient throat—illustrating a real-world mechanical texture hazard of fibrous citrus segments in dysphagia without constituting clinical trial evidence.

Unknown (Researched): although retrospective interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) surveys frequently list acidic citrus fruits among self-reported symptom triggers (Shorter 2007, PMID:17499305, n=104; Bassaly 2011, n=598), high-level prospective and systematic evidence directly contradicts a consistent worsening effect. A 2025 PROSPERO systematic review of 51 bladder-irritant studies (Ha et al., PMID:40105788, including 27 caffeinated/carbonated/citrus studies) concluded there is NO consistent evidence linking citrus or other candidate irritants to overactive bladder or urinary urgency, and the prospective 5-year BACH cohort (Maserejian 2013, PMID:23722012, n=4,144) actually found citrus juice associated with 50% LOWER odds of LUTS progression in men (p=0.02) and no worsening in women. Furthermore, CYP3A4 inhibition of OAB antimuscarinics (oxybutynin, solifenacin, darifenacin; Pasko 2016, PMID:27738922) increases anticholinergic exposure rather than directly worsening urgency, and zero trials test raw grapefruit in Parkinson urinary urgency.

Unknown (Researched): No clinical trial evaluates raw grapefruit on visual hallucinations or Parkinson psychosis. While CYP3A4 inhibition can precipitate quetiapine overdose toxicity (Cinderella 2021, PMID:34608881) and raise cabergoline levels (Nagai 2005, n=5 PD without adverse events), repeated grapefruit juice does NOT alter CYP1A2-metabolized clozapine plasma levels or antipsychotic efficacy (Lane 2001, PMID:11816871), and no study measures hallucination frequency.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial evaluates raw grapefruit on Parkinson walking slowness or gait speed (consistent with Round 1 shortened stride 0853 = Unknown). Nagai 2005 (n=5 PD cabergoline PK) omitted gait outcomes, and rodent neurotoxin studies used isolated nootkatone/limonin/naringin rather than raw fruit.

Unknown (Researched): No oral culinary cold-pressed grapeseed oil trial assesses apathy; Irandoost 2013 (PMID:23506314, n=44) measured only hs-CRP and HOMA-IR, and aromatherapy trials use unscented grapeseed oil purely as an inert topical/olfactory control.

Unknown (Researched): No oral culinary refined grapeseed oil trial tests human attention. Du et al. 2022 (PMID:34709668, n=59) tested INHALED airborne particulate emissions from an ultrasonic office diffuser (exposure_fit=unusable for dietary refined oil), and Berahmand 2020 (PMC7335983) tested oral cold-pressed oil in a scopolamine rat spatial-memory model without attention endpoints.

Unknown (Researched): No human or Parkinson animal trial tests oral cold-pressed culinary grapeseed oil on bradykinesia. Aqueous/hydroalcoholic grape seed polyphenol extract (GSPE/GSE) trials are chemically distinct defatted-pomace extracts (exposure_fit=unusable) and cannot be conflated with culinary seed oil.

Unknown (Researched): No oral culinary cold-pressed grapeseed oil trial reports daytime sleepiness. The Healthy Cookie Study (NCT02841618, 10 g/d grapeseed oil cookie) registered an unspecified secondary sleep questionnaire correlation without posted results, and NCT04648215 used grapeseed oil strictly as a bedside gauze aroma placebo.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial, observational study, or animal experiment tests dietary refined grapeseed oil on drooling or sialorrhea; human oral trials evaluate only metabolic/platelet biomarkers (Irandoost 2013, Lyte 2016, Bazan-Salinas 2016).

Unknown (Researched): No oral culinary refined grapeseed oil study evaluates Parkinson levodopa-induced dyskinesia. Benvegnu et al. 2018 (PMID:29209877) injected haloperidol-loaded grapeseed-oil nanocapsules intraperitoneally in rats (parenteral drug excipient, exposure_fit=unusable for oral culinary oil).

Unknown (Researched): No oral culinary refined grapeseed oil trial tests executive function. Du et al. 2022 (PMID:34709668, n=59) exposed office students to INHALED airborne particulate matter from an ultrasonic grapeseed-oil diffuser (worsening response inhibition via PM inhalation—exposure_fit=unusable for ingested culinary oil), while Berahmand 2020 (PMC7335983) tested scopolamine rat spatial memory rather than executive function.

Unknown (Researched): No oral culinary cold-pressed grapeseed oil trial measures fatigue. The Healthy Cookie Energy Study (NCT04677920, n=24) evaluates skeletal-muscle cardiolipin/mitochondria with no posted fatigue results, and Irandoost 2013 (n=44) measured only hs-CRP and insulin resistance.

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial or Parkinson model tests oral cold-pressed grapeseed oil on freezing of gait. The Healthy Cookie Study (NCT02841618) lists secondary gait speed correlation in healthy adults with no posted results and no freezing-of-gait endpoint.
Unknown (Researched): Zero clinical, observational, or preclinical studies evaluate oral refined grapeseed oil on Parkinson hypophonia or voice loudness.

Unknown (Researched): No oral culinary refined grapeseed oil study tests Parkinson muscle rigidity. STRICT MATRIX SEPARATION: Sarkaki 2012 (PMC4075680, 6-OHDA rat rigidity) tested hydroalcoholic grape seed polyphenol extract (GSE), NOT culinary refined grapeseed oil (linoleic-acid lipid matrix; exposure_fit=unusable). Parkinson UK forum threads (2009) mention culinary grapeseed oil strictly as a topical arm-massage glide carrier for stiffness, not dietary consumption.

Unknown (Researched): No oral culinary cold-pressed grapeseed oil study evaluates olfactory function in Parkinson disease; Snow et al. 2004 (PMID:15253846) used unscented grapeseed oil solely as an odorless sachet control in dementia aromatherapy.

Unknown (Researched): No oral culinary refined grapeseed oil clinical trial measures blood pressure, orthostatic hypotension, or lightheadedness; human dietary trials test hs-CRP/insulin resistance (Irandoost 2013, n=44), postprandial endotoxin (Lyte 2016, n=20, null vs olive oil), and platelet aggregation (Bazan-Salinas 2016, n=30).

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial or PD model evaluates oral refined grapeseed oil on postural stability or balance; NCT02841618 registered healthy-adult gait/grip correlations without balance outcomes or posted results.
Unknown (Researched): Zero clinical, observational, or cultural sources evaluate dietary refined grapeseed oil on Parkinson hypomimia (reduced facial expressiveness).

Carried-forward Round 1 rodent studies (Uket 2024, Kaur & Saxena 2022) did not test culinary cooked green pods in humans or PD neuropsychiatric scales, and the recent 2026 human green-bean feeding trial (Finlay 2026, n=27) measured only urinary intake biomarkers.

Direct brewed green tea evidence in Parkinson's disease is null for anxiety: Chen 2015 (n=14 PD, 3 cups/d brewed green tea x 3 mo, uncontrolled) showed non-significant BAI change (10.3 -> 9.3), and Sakakima 2026 (n=78 daily PD green tea drinkers, cross-sectional) showed a completely null anxious-mood correlation (r=-0.12, p=0.294). Across non-PD RCTs, Loftis 2013 (n=34 EGCG DB-RCT) was null on anxiety, the 2026 Molecular Psychiatry meta-analysis of 31 L-theanine RCTs (Gerolymos 2026 n=1,168) concluded that anxiety effects were inconsistent and non-significant, and Unno 2017/2024 demonstrated that caffeine and EGCG in standard hot-brewed green tea actively counteract L-theanine's stress-relieving effect. Community reports (Parkinson's UK 2020) are likewise mixed/no-effect, keeping this claim open (Unknown).

Direct Parkinson's data for brewed green tea and apathy are completely null: in Sakakima 2026 (n=78 daily PD green tea drinkers, Table 4), daily green tea volume had zero favorable association with MDS-UPDRS apathy (Spearman r=+0.06, p=0.614). Neither Chen 2015 (n=14 PD brewed green tea) nor Chan 2009 (NCT00461942 n=410 green tea polyphenols) reported apathy outcomes, leaving the claim open (Unknown).

Acute randomized controlled human trials of green tea and its co-occurring L-theanine + caffeine matrix demonstrate modest short-term easing—opposing the frozen worsening claim—of attention impairment in non-PD adults: Dietz 2017 (n=23 single-blind crossover) showed 4 g matcha green tea drink significantly improved acute basic attention abilities and psychomotor speed at 60 min vs placebo; Baba 2021 (n=50 older adults 50-69 y DB-RCT) showed single-dose L-theanine improved Stroop Part 1 attention reaction time (though 12-week regular intake was null); and recent meta-analyses confirm acute attention gains (Payne 2025 SR/MA of 50 RCTs: L-theanine+caffeine attention-switching accuracy h2 SMD 0.33 [0.13-0.54] and digit vigilance SMD 0.20 [0.02-0.38], including brewed tea crossovers; Gerolymos 2026 MA of 31 RCTs choice RT SMD 0.51; Mátyus 2025 recognition visual RT -15.20 ms). Crucial adversarial/chronic limits cap confidence strictly at minimal_signal (50.005, Maybe False): chronic >=3-wk trials are NULL (Uchida 2024 n=99 12-mo triple-blind matcha RCT: complex attention p=0.875, simple attention p=0.181; Marsh 2026 chronic Camellia sinensis SR null), Café-PD 2017 (n=118 PD) saw slight global MoCA decline (-0.66 pts) under chronic 400 mg/d isolated caffeine capsules, and no controlled PD brewed green tea attention trial exists.

Consistent with Round 1 brewed black tea (0082), a double-blind placebo-controlled Parkinson's trial of isolated caffeine capsules (Postuma 2012, PMID:22855866, n=61 PD) directly isolated the UPDRS Part III bradykinesia subscore and found a statistically significant 6-week reduction of -1.70 points (95% CI -3.10 to -0.31; limb-only CI crossed zero), opposing worsening. Infusion chemistry confirms caffeine (~30-50 mg/cup, lower than 200-400 mg/d trial capsules) in standard brewed green tea (Unno 2017 PMC5537891; Chen 2015). Competing/tempering evidence includes the larger 6-18 month Café-PD trial (Postuma 2017 n=118 PD) finding null total MDS-UPDRS III (-0.48, 95% CI -3.21 to 2.25, suggesting possible tachyphylaxis), Chen 2015 (n=14 uncontrolled PD brewed green tea: UPDRS III motor 21.2->18.1 p<0.05 but UPDRS II ADL 9.2->9.9 p<0.05 without isolating bradykinesia), and Chan 2009 (NCT00461942 n=410 early PD green tea polyphenols: 6-mo total UPDRS lift with null 12-mo difference and no item breakdown). Because the direct PD bradykinesia RCT used isolated caffeine capsules rather than brewed green tea, evidence qualifies for limited_clinical_link (51, eases -> Maybe False).

Clinical evidence for brewed green tea on chronic or Parkinson's constipation is inconclusive and heavily confounded. In Sakakima 2026 (n=78 daily PD green tea drinkers, cross-sectional), the overall three-group comparison for moderate/severe constipation across <500 mL, 500-1000 mL, and >1000 mL/day was NOT statistically significant (20/42, 4/12, 5/24; p=0.144); although post-hoc Spearman (r=-0.28, p=0.018) and adjusted OR (0.71, 0.50-0.99) reached nominal significance, the study did not record water or total fluid intake—creating major hydration confounding—and was industry-funded. Surgical RCT evidence is also conflicting and non-chronic: Liu 2021 (n=77 open-label gastrectomy RCT) reported faster postoperative flatus/defecation vs water, whereas Watanabe 2024 (n=18 colon surgery pilot RCT) found brewed green tea completely NULL on time to first defecation (42.0 vs 49.4 h, p=0.79). No chronic functional or Parkinson's constipation RCT of brewed green tea exists (Unknown).

No human clinical trial has evaluated brewed green tea on daily OFF time in Parkinson's disease. Preclinical biochemical and animal studies (Kang 2010 PMID:20700524; Kang 2013; Lin 2021; Zhou 2024) show isolated EGCG and tea catechins can inhibit COMT-mediated levodopa methylation in vitro and in rodents/rabbits, but catechins can also chelate iron and have uncertain human levodopa bioavailability interactions. In human Parkinson's data, a 2025 meta-analysis of n=3,346 PD patients (Huang 2025 PMID:40451127) found NO significant association between caffeine intake and motor fluctuations, and Café-PD 2017 did not demonstrate reduced OFF time. Evidence remains open (Unknown).

Consistent with Round 2 brewed black tea (0618) and Round 3 brewed coffee (0605), two multicenter double-blind placebo-controlled Parkinson's trials of isolated caffeine capsules—bridged to brewed green tea via measured infusion caffeine (~30-50 mg/cup, Unno 2017 PMC5537891)—demonstrate modest, attenuating reductions in PD daytime sleepiness: Postuma 2012 (n=61 somnolent PD) improved CGI-C somnolence (+0.64, 95% CI 0.16 to 1.13) and per-protocol ESS (-1.97, -3.87 to -0.05; primary ITT ESS -1.71, -3.57 to 0.13), and Café-PD (Postuma 2017 n=118 analyzed PD) lowered 6-month MDS-UPDRS 1.8 daytime sleepiness (-0.49, -0.79 to -0.20) and 3-month SCOPA-sleep daytime (-1.09, -1.88 to -0.30) before attenuating at 12-18 months. Important direct green-tea tempering evidence shows NULL ESS change in non-somnolent cohorts: Chen 2015 (n=14 uncontrolled PD, baseline ESS 7.8 -> 7.7) and Baba 2024 (n=46 non-PD matcha 71.5 mg caffeine RCT, ESS -2.0 vs -2.9, p=0.54). Because the two positive PD RCTs administered higher-dose isolated caffeine capsules rather than brewed green tea, evidence qualifies for limited_clinical_link (51, eases -> Maybe True).

Direct Parkinson's brewed green tea evidence is completely NULL for depressive symptoms: in Chen 2015 (n=14 PD, 3 cups/d brewed green tea x 3 mo, uncontrolled) mean Beck Depression Inventory slightly rose (7.1 -> 7.9, NS), and in Sakakima 2026 (n=78 daily PD green tea drinkers) MDS-UPDRS depressed mood showed zero association with daily green tea volume (Spearman r=-0.03, p=0.772). Moreover, non-PD randomized trials of tea catechins/matcha were also null or marginal (Loftis 2013 n=34 EGCG DB-RCT null; Dietz 2017 n=23 matcha POMS null; Baba 2024 n=46 matcha BDI-II trend p<0.1 only), and the 2022 meta-analysis of observational studies (Yaegashi 2022) found a NULL prospective cohort subgroup (OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.04-2.14). Although Dong 2022 (n=7,524 prospective cohort, HR 0.78), Chen 2022 (n=10,014 cross-sectional Guangzhou Biobank), and Shamabadi 2023 (n=50 MDD adjunct high-dose isolated L-theanine 200 mg/d + sertraline, p=0.014) reported favorable associations/constituent signals, the two null direct PD brewed-tea studies plus null EGCG/matcha RCTs balance them, keeping the brewed green tea claim open (Unknown).

No completed clinical trial or observational study has tested brewed green tea on REM sleep behavior disorder or dream enactment frequency in Parkinson's disease. A recruiting trial protocol (NCT07682532) combines L-theanine with a Mediterranean diet in PD with RBD endpoints but has no posted results.

No clinical trial or observational study has evaluated brewed green tea on Parkinson's drooling (sialorrhea). Chen 2015 (n=14 PD brewed green tea) and Chan 2009 (n=410 polyphenols) did not isolate salivation/drooling subscores.

Consistent with Round 2 brewed black tea (0622) and Round 3 brewed coffee (0609), the multicenter double-blind Café-PD trial (Postuma 2017, PMID:28954882, n=118 analyzed PD, caffeine 200 mg BID vs placebo—bridged to brewed green tea via measured infusion caffeine in Unno 2017 PMC5537891) directly measured dyskinesia severity and demonstrated statistically significant worsening on MDS-UPDRS 4.1+4.2 across combined timepoints (+0.25 pts, 95% CI 0.04 to 0.45; +0.28 [0.01 to 0.55] at 3 mo; +0.36 [0.02 to 0.70] at 18 mo), supported by an early PD clinical challenge (Shoulson & Chase 1975 n=6). Competing/tempering evidence includes null 6-week dyskinesia in Postuma 2012 (n=61, only 14/61 with baseline dyskinesia), null caffeine association with motor fluctuations in Huang 2025 MA (n=3,346 PD), and an observational CALM-PD coffee analysis (Wills 2013 HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.37-1.01, crossing 1.0). Because Café-PD tested higher-dose isolated caffeine capsules rather than brewed green tea, evidence qualifies for limited_clinical_link (51, worsens -> Maybe True).

No clinical trial has evaluated brewed green tea on Parkinson's dystonia severity. Neither Chen 2015 (n=14 brewed green tea), Chan 2009 (n=410 polyphenols), nor Postuma 2012/2017 (isolated caffeine) isolated dystonia outcomes.

Recent adversarial long-term green tea randomized trials and meta-analyses are NULL on executive function: Uchida 2024 (PMC11364242, n=99 older adults 12-month triple-blind matcha RCT) found no effect on executive function (p=0.438), cognitive flexibility (p=0.379), or MoCA-J (p=0.175); Marsh 2026 (PMC12935010) found chronic >=3-wk Camellia sinensis RCTs null; Mátyus 2025 meta-analysis found L-theanine NULL on Stroop executive interference (-37.38 ms, 95% CI -86.39 to 11.62); PENSA 2025 (n=129 APOE4 SCD) missed its primary PACC-exe executive/cognitive composite with EGCG + lifestyle (p=0.061); and Café-PD 2017 (n=118 PD) saw slight global MoCA decline (-0.66 pts) under chronic isolated caffeine. Acute attention-switching gains in black tea/L-theanine crossovers (De Bruin 2011; Payne 2025) are balanced by these direct chronic green tea/matcha/EGCG executive nulls and absence of PD brewed green tea executive data, leaving this claim open (Unknown).

No clinical trial has assessed brewed green tea on fall frequency in Parkinson's disease. Although pre-meal brewed green tea attenuated acute postprandial BP drops in non-PD older adults (Son 2012), falls were never measured.

No controlled clinical trial has tested brewed green tea on freezing of gait (FOG) in Parkinson's disease. An uncontrolled historical Japanese abstract of isolated oral caffeine 100 mg/d (Kitagawa 2007, PMID:17373724) described transient improvement in akinetic FOG with tolerance developing over months, but lacked control arm, verified sample size, and brewed green tea administration, while controlled PD caffeine trials (Postuma 2012; Café-PD 2017) did not isolate FOG improvement.

No controlled trial has isolated hand dexterity (e.g., pegboard or UPDRS finger-tapping/hand-movement subscores) under brewed green tea in Parkinson's disease. Chen 2015 (n=14 uncontrolled) reported only composite UPDRS III/II without hand-dexterity breakdown.

Clinical evidence for brewed green tea and insomnia is directly conflicted and timing-/dose-dependent. Worsening signals include Chan 2009 (NCT00461942, n=410 early PD delayed-start RCT of concentrated green tea polyphenols reporting slightly more insomnia than placebo in funder summary, without full peer-reviewed data), Unno 2017 (n=19 crossover: standard caffeinated brewed green tea increased early-morning awakening B2 WASO vs low-caffeine brew, though overall SL, TST, WASO, and sleep efficiency 88.5% vs 89.2% did not differ significantly), and a 2013 Parkinson's UK patient report of waking 4-5x/night after starting green tea. Credible opposing/null evidence directly balances this: Sakakima 2026 (n=78 daily PD green tea drinkers) found HIGHER daily green tea intake was inversely associated with MDS-UPDRS nighttime sleep disturbances (three-group p=0.029, r=-0.35 p=0.002, adjusted OR 0.57 [0.39-0.83]), Baba 2024 (n=46 DB-RCT of 2.7 g/d matcha capsules delivering 71.5 mg caffeine) showed NO objective EEG sleep disruption and shorter post-wake time in bed (p=0.04), Uchida 2024 (n=99 12-mo matcha RCT) trended toward BETTER PSQI (p=0.088), and a 2019 Parkinson's UK participant reported sleeping soundly even after midnight green tea. Because opposing clinical PD and RCT signals balance each other, the claim remains open (Unknown), with a practical clinical note that caffeine-sensitive PD patients may experience sleep disruption from evening caffeinated brews.
No clinical study has evaluated brewed green tea on Parkinson's hypophonia or low voice volume severity.

Consistent with Round 2 brewed black tea (0631) and Round 3 brewed coffee (0617), a double-blind placebo-controlled Parkinson's trial of isolated caffeine capsules (Postuma 2012, PMID:22855866, n=61 PD) directly isolated the UPDRS Part III rigidity subcomponent and reported a statistically significant 6-week reduction of -1.01 points (published 95% CI -2.0 to -0.7) alongside total UPDRS III (-3.15), bridged to brewed green tea via verified infusion caffeine (~30-50 mg/cup, Unno 2017 PMC5537891). Tempering evidence includes the larger 6-18 month Café-PD trial (Postuma 2017 n=118 PD) showing null total MDS-UPDRS III (-0.48, 95% CI -3.21 to 2.25; rigidity subscore not isolated), uncontrolled Chen 2015 (n=14 PD brewed green tea: UPDRS III 21.2->18.1, UPDRS II 9.2->9.9, no rigidity breakdown), and Chan 2009 (NCT00461942 n=410 polyphenols: composite UPDRS only, 12-mo null). Because the direct PD rigidity RCT used isolated caffeine capsules rather than brewed green tea, evidence qualifies for limited_clinical_link (51, eases -> Maybe True).

Two older-adult human clinical studies demonstrate acute pre-meal pressor attenuation of postprandial and standing blood-pressure drops with brewed tea—opposing the frozen worsening claim: Son & Lee 2012 (PMID:22329391, n=29 older adults with postprandial hypotension >=15 mmHg SBP drop) showed 400 mL brewed green tea before lunch elicited acute pressor effects (+15.1 mmHg SBP and +5.7 mmHg DBP over 90 min post-lunch vs no tea), and Rakic 1996 (PMID:8800584, n=171 older-adult RCT) showed brewed tea attenuated postprandial drops in both supine SBP (3.8 +/- 1.2 mmHg, p=0.029) and standing SBP (5.2 +/- 2.1 mmHg), echoed by a 2023 scoping review (Huang 2023). Competing/tempering context includes modest chronic resting BP lowering in non-hypotensive/hypertensive adults across green tea meta-analyses (Yıldırım Ayaz 2023 n=680: -2.99/-0.95 mmHg; Li 2015 n=971: -1.42/-1.25 mmHg), absence of direct lightheadedness symptom severity ratings, and lack of a Parkinson's neurogenic orthostatic hypotension RCT. Evidence therefore qualifies strictly for minimal_signal (50.005, eases -> Maybe False).

One randomized trial directly testing brewed Laoshan green tea versus water in 77 post-gastrectomy patients (Liu et al. 2021, PMC8563416) reported lower postoperative VAS pain scores on days 1-4 alongside standard flurbiprofen axetil analgesia, supported by a 16-week RCT of oral green tea extract in 194 adults with diabetic peripheral neuropathy (Essmat & Hussein 2021, PMID:33517103) showing reduced sensorineural VAS pain and TCSS scores at weeks 8 and 16. Significant tempering and adversarial limits hold confidence strictly at minimal_signal (50.005, Maybe True): Liu 2021 was open-label with retrospective registration, acute surgical pain, and NSAID co-therapy; Essmat 2021 tested concentrated green tea extract capsules rather than brewed tea; Hashempur 2018 (n=50 knee OA open-label RCT of oral GTE + diclofenac) showed mixed pain outcomes (VAS pain p=0.038, but WOMAC pain subscale NULL p=0.163); Oliveira 2023 (n=42 topical GTE+HA gel) was null on palatal pain; and zero Parkinson's pain RCTs of brewed green tea exist.

No clinical trial has evaluated brewed green tea on postural instability or pull-test balance in Parkinson's disease. Neither Chen 2015, Chan 2009, nor Postuma 2012/2017 isolated postural instability improvement.
No clinical study has evaluated brewed green tea on hypomimia or reduced facial expressiveness in Parkinson's disease.

Evidence for brewed green tea and Parkinson's rest tremor is genuinely inconclusive and mixed across directions. In Postuma 2012 (n=61 PD isolated caffeine RCT), UPDRS-III rest tremor estimates were small with 95% confidence intervals spanning zero at both week 3 (-0.32, 95% CI -0.73 to 0.10) and week 6 (-0.28, -0.83 to 0.27); neither Chen 2015 (n=14 PD brewed green tea) nor Chan 2009 (n=410 green tea polyphenols) reported rest tremor item scores. Conversely, caffeine dose-escalation in PD (Altman 2011) noted tremor worsening among discontinuation reasons, Koller 1987 reported 6% of PD survey respondents perceived worse tremor with coffee (without acute challenge increase), Köhler 2026 (PMID:43080293) confirmed caffeine enhances physiological tremor amplitude, and public PD forums contain opposing anecdotes (2025 Reddit report of worsened arm tremor with coffee/green tea vs 2018 Parkinson's UK thread 12093 adding green tea alongside Mucuna pruriens levodopa). Because randomized rest-tremor confidence intervals cross zero and opposing physiological/experiential worsening signals exist, this claim remains open (Unknown).

No clinical study has evaluated brewed green tea on stride length in Parkinson's disease. Makizako 2026 (n=78 older adults) showed null overall physical performance with catechin green tea + exercise, and PD trials omitted stride measurements.
No clinical study has evaluated brewed green tea on dysarthria or speech intelligibility impairment in Parkinson's disease.
No clinical study has evaluated brewed green tea on Parkinson's dysphagia or swallowing difficulty severity.

Although high-dose total caffeine reduction RCTs in overactive bladder adults (Bryant 2002 n=95: urgency p=0.002, frequency p=0.037; Park 2023 SR of 8 studies) and high-dose urodynamic caffeine challenge (Lohsiriwat 2011 n=12, 4.5 mg/kg caffeine) show high caffeine intakes can trigger urinary urgency, NO clinical trial has directly shown moderate-caffeine brewed green tea (~30-50 mg/cup) worsens urinary urgency. Directly opposing tea-specific clinical and epidemiologic data balance caffeine extrapolation: Katz 2014 (n=46 men DB-RCT) found a green+black tea polyphenol extract capsule (AssuriTEA 1000 mg/d x 12 wk) significantly IMPROVED lower urinary tract symptoms (AUAss -34.5%, p=0.008), Wen 2015 (n=9,637 Chinese adults >=40 y) found NO correlation between habitual tea consumption and nocturia, and Sun 2016 MA / Townsend 2012 NHS found no general caffeine-incontinence progression. Given low-to-moderate caffeine in brewed green tea, null tea epidemiology, and opposite tea-polyphenol LUTS data, the claim remains open (Unknown), while advising PD patients with OAB to monitor personal sensitivity to caffeinated tea.

Direct Parkinson's data for brewed green tea and hallucinations are null: in Sakakima 2026 (n=78 daily PD green tea drinkers, Table 4), daily green tea volume showed NO statistically significant association with MDS-UPDRS hallucinations and psychosis (Spearman r=-0.11, p=0.360). Neither Chen 2015 (n=14 PD brewed green tea) nor Chan 2009 (NCT00461942 n=410) reported visual hallucination endpoints, leaving this claim open (Unknown).

No controlled Parkinson's trial demonstrates brewed green tea eases or worsens walking slowness. In community-dwelling older adults, Makizako 2026 (PMID:42030620, n=78 RCT) found catechin-enriched green tea combined with exercise showed NO overall physical performance or walking-speed superiority over control. In Parkinson's disease, Sakakima 2026 included walking speed only in unadjusted descriptive comparisons without a causal brewed-tea effect, Chen 2015 (n=14 uncontrolled) reported composite UPDRS III/II without walking speed, and Café-PD 2017 (n=118 isolated caffeine) showed null total MDS-UPDRS III (-0.48) without gait-speed improvement. Evidence remains open (Unknown).

No controlled clinical study isolates raw guava fruit (Psidium guajava) for anxiety severity in Parkinson's disease. Full-text OA inspection of a 2026 8-week pilot RCT of boiled unripe pink guava juice jelly drink in 73 healthy working-age adults (Nguyen 2026, PMID:42511208, PMC13409673) found active arms substituted mint syrup (4.84-9.68%) for placebo honey syrup (co-intervention confounding), and 2-month HADS-Anxiety was virtually identical between low-dose (3.87 +/- 2.69) and placebo (3.88 +/- 2.24; reported p=0.033 reflected within-group regression from a higher baseline of 5.00; high-dose p=0.052). Preclinical anxiolytic rodent studies (Harithadevi 2024 PMID:39350921; Sahoo 2021) tested guava LEAF extracts in non-PD stress/withdrawal models rather than raw guava fruit, leaving anxiety severity Unknown (Researched).

No human clinical trial, observational cohort, or Parkinson's disease animal model evaluates raw guava fruit (Psidium guajava) for apathy severity. A 2026 pilot RCT of boiled guava juice + mint syrup jelly drink in healthy working-age adults (Nguyen 2026, PMC13409673) did not assess apathy severity and was confounded by mint-vs-honey co-intervention, while traditional Mayan CNS reviews (Castañeda 2022) provide no clinical raw-fruit data. Strict separation of raw fruit from guava leaf extracts leaves apathy severity Unknown (Researched).

No controlled clinical study establishes that raw guava fruit worsens or eases attention impairment in Parkinson's disease. A 140-day cluster RCT of 25 g/d fresh raw guava fruit in 399 Indian preschoolers (Roy Choudhury 2021, PMID:33385184; corroborated by Roberts 2022 systematic review, PMID:35276891) improved iron biomarkers but found NO impact on cognitive development. Rodent whole-nut memory studies (Bahaeddin 2017, Olofinnade 2021) and isolated peptide YYLLVR in hypertensive rats (Song 2026) are non-PD preclinical models.

Maybe False (51): Contrary to the frozen claim that cooked herring reduces daily OFF time, four controlled Parkinson's disease protein/LNAA clinical trials consistently show that daytime high-protein animal meals compete with levodopa transport across gut and blood-brain barrier LAT1 transporters and INCREASE daily OFF time in levodopa-treated fluctuators—Barichella 2006 (PMID:16773618, n=18 crossover: low-protein vs normal daytime protein reduced postprandial OFF by -107 min, P=0.0005, and 24-h OFF by -114 min, P=0.0009), Tsui 1989 (PMID:2494567, n=10 blinded crossover), Carter 1989 (PMID:2648188, n=5), and Eriksson 1988 (PMID:3135513, n=11). Analytically, Atlantic herring (Wu 2022, PMC9636446: up to 19.2% ww protein, 43.3% essential amino acids rich in leucine, valine, isoleucine, phenylalanine, tyrosine) and Baltic herring fillets (Kakko 2022, PMC8775156: EAA/NEAA 0.77) deliver high-density animal LNAAs, and human crossover kinetics confirm fish meals raise plasma LNAAs comparably to beef/chicken (Uhe 1992, PMID:1542005). Tempering context: sensitivity affects a subset rather than every PD patient (Virmani 2016, PMC4881294, n=1,037: 12.4% overall, higher in fluctuators; Nutt 1989), and structured protein redistribution/dose spacing can mitigate interference (Pinelli 2024, PMID:36786430, n=51).

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial has measured standing/tilt-table orthostatic blood-pressure drops or orthostatic lightheadedness after brewed Hibiscus sabdariffa tea in Parkinson's disease or any other population. Replicated non-PD RCTs demonstrate substantial resting systemic blood-pressure lowering from brewed hibiscus tea/infusions in hypertensive adults—McKay 2010 (PMID:20018807, n=65 DB-RCT: SBP -7.2 vs -1.3 mmHg, P=0.030), Jalalyazdi 2019 (PMC6621350, n=46 RCT: SBP -7.43 vs -1.91 P=0.004, DBP -6.70 vs -3.96 P<0.001), Mozaffari-Khosravi 2009 (PMID:18685605, n=60 T2D mild HTN: SBP 134.4->112.7 mmHg, P<0.001), Bourqui 2021 (PMID:32948827, n=219 Senegal RCT, 10 g/d bissap brew: SBP -20.7 mmHg ~ captopril), Herrera-Arellano 2004 (PMID:15330492, n=75), Nwachukwu 2015 (PMID:26289514, n=80 vs HCTZ/placebo, P<0.001), plus healthy-adult crossover Chiu 2022 (PMID:35758855, n=39, 6 mo roselle drink) and syntheses Ellis 2022 (PMC9086798, 17 RCTs: SBP -7.10/-10.05 mmHg) and Norouzzadeh 2025 (26 RCTs, n=1,797). However, consistent with Round 4 calibration for garlic (0380) and flaxseed (0328) and rubric outcome-fit rules, resting BP reductions without postural or symptomatic hypotension endpoints remain a remote proxy: BP drops scale inversely with baseline BP (r=-0.421 in McKay 2010), trials reported no orthostatic dizziness or adverse-event elevation, acute single-dose crossovers were NULL (Abubakar 2019 PMC6412462; Ellis 2025 PMID:40009760), a 2025 Thai MetS DB-RCT was NULL (Chaisungnern 2025, n=108), and Cochrane 2021 (Pattanittum, PMC8626866) rated certainty very low. Clinical caution: PD patients with neurogenic orthostatic hypotension should monitor standing BP when consuming regular antihypertensive doses of brewed hibiscus.

No human clinical trial or Parkinson's disease animal model evaluates raw honeydew melon (Cucumis melo Inodorus) for anxiety severity.
